# Image act, then type act

Cinetic ecfa6605de1adb9345ce937724810dc32267d068 · MIT · ps-image-act-then-type-act
Reference data: engine APIs in this source are examples, not Syka instructions.

Category: pacing_structure; energy: medium; role: workhorse; formats: feature, vertical

## Mechanism
A short spot splits in half: the first half is pure imagery with no words at all, the second is pure type with no imagery.

## Use when
6-12 s spots and social cut-downs with one claim and a strong visual metaphor, especially when watched on mute.

## Avoid when
Product walkthroughs that need captions on the UI, and films over 20 s.

## Original recipe (adapt to Syka native time and nodes)
Storyboard two contiguous ACTs at about 47/53%. Act 1 is three image shots of about 80 f each with no text layer at all, each ending on an accelerating exit (E.in). Act 2 is type only on a plain stage: the claim, then the headline, then the CTA and the lockup. Its first card continues act 1's screen direction across the seam. Keep text and imagery in separate Sequences so neither act can leak into the other, and run each type card on the breath envelope.

## Original timing
Total 480-600 f. Act 1: 3 shots of 70-90 f. Act 2: claim 70-80 f, headline 60-70 f, CTA 60 f, then lockup 90-110 f.
